chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about raisins, how to cook them so that their drink is permissible. He said: 'Take a quarter of raisins, clean them, then pour twelve ratls of water over them, then soak them overnight. When it is the next day, remove their foam, then pour water over them sufficient to submerge them, then boil them with fire until they boil, then remove their water and pour it over the first water.'

Then place it all in one vessel, then light a fire beneath it until two-thirds of it evaporates and one-third remains, with the fire still beneath it. Then take a ratl of honey, boil it with fire until it boils, and remove its foam. Then place it upon the cooked mixture, then stir it until it mixes with it. And if you wish, add saffron to it, and if you wish, flavor it with a little ginger.

He said: 'So if you want to divide it into three parts to cook it, measure it with one thing until you know how much it is. Then place the first part in the vessel in which you boil it, then make a measurement and mark it where the water reaches. Then place the other third, then mark it where the water reaches. Then place the final third, then mark it where the last one reaches. Then ignite a gentle fire beneath it until two-thirds of it evaporates and one-third remains.'
ai.seo_question: How to prepare raisin drink so it is halal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the precise culinary and legal methodology for preparing 'Zabib' (raisin drink/vinegar) by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing the control of fermentation through specific boiling and reduction ratios to ensure it remains Halal. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking practical domestic arts with fiqh, illustrating how minor variations in preparation can determine the permissibility of consumables. The inclusion of honey and optional spices like saffron or ginger highlights the balance between preservation, taste, and ritual purity in early Islamic society.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Al Sabatany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the raisins, how to cook it until its drink is Permissible.

So heasws said: ‘Take a quarter of raisins, so clean these. Then pour twelve ratls (units of measurement) of water over it, then soak it overnight. So when it is the morning, remove its foam, then pour sufficient water over it to submerge it. Then boil it by the fire with a boiling. Then remove its water and pour over it the first water.

Then place it all in one vessel, then light a fire beneath it until two-thirds of it evaporates and there remains the third, and under it is the fire. Then take a ratl (unit of measurement) of honey and boil it by the fire with a boiling, and remove its foam. Then place it upon the cooking, then stir it until it is mixed, and place in it, if you so desire to, saffron, and if you so desire to aromatise it by a little ginger’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So if you want to divide it into three in order to cook it, so measure it with one thing until you know how much it is. Then place over it the first in the vessel which it is boiled in, then you should make a measurement and its mark where the water reaches. Then place the other third, then mark it where the water reaches. Then place the other third, then mark it when the last reaches. Then ignite a small fire beneath it (low heat) until two-thirds of it evaporates and there remains one-third of it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar al-Sabatiy who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about raisins and how to cook them to become clean for drinking.

He (the Imam) said, ‘Take one quarter of raisins and clean it. Thereafter pour twelve ritl of water on it, then leave it for the night to soak. In the morning remove its suds, then pour on it enough water so it is covered thereby. Thereafter, boil it on fire for a boil then remove the water, then pour it on the first water, then place all of it in one pot.

Then, ignite fire beneath it until two- thirds are evaporated and only one-third has remained with the fire underneath. Then take one ritl of honey and boil it on fire for a boil, remove its blur, pour it on the cooked (preparation), beat it until it is mixed, then pour saffron or a little ginger for fragrance.

“You can also divide it in three parts to cook. First, you should measure it by a certain measurement so you know how much it is. Then place the first one in a pot in which you want to boil it. Then pour in it one-third as much as water reaches and mark its level, then pour the other third part, then mark it where water reaches then pour the last third part, then mark it where this other reaches; then fire underneath gently until its two-thirds are gone and only one-third is left.’”
